**8B.10 Research Note: Shehbaz Sharif in 2024**

**Overall read**
By end-2024, Sharif was **somewhat closer** to his revealed economic and state-capacity program than at the start of the year. The clearest gains were macro stabilization, technocratic staffing, and some delivery reform. But the gains were **fragile and incomplete**, and the domestic political track moved the other way: tighter controls on opposition, media, courts, and protest. On balance, the evidence supports “closer, but unevenly and not durably.”

**Accepted Claims**

- **IMF says growth returned, inflation fell, reserves rebuilt**
  - Publisher: IMF
  - Date: 2024-09-27
  - URL: [https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr)
  - Claim: Pakistan had restored macro stability by late 2024, with growth back, inflation down, reserve buffers rebuilt, and external pressures eased. This is the strongest evidence that Sharif ended the year closer to his stabilization program than he began.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`, `7B.10`

- **World Bank says FY24 growth recovered, but poverty still rose**
  - Publisher: World Bank
  - Date: 2024-10-10
  - URL: [https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank)
  - Claim: The economy improved versus the starting point, but the recovery was not broad-based because poverty still increased. This supports “closer than at the start,” but only on a partial, fragile basis.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`, `7B.10`

- **IMF says the new program aimed to entrench macro stability and fairer rules**
  - Publisher: IMF
  - Date: 2024-09-27
  - URL: [https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr)
  - Claim: The government’s agenda by late 2024 was explicitly framed around macro stability, stronger competition, SOE reform, and a fairer business environment. That is direct evidence of programmatic movement, even though implementation was incomplete.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `7B.10`

- **Sharif announced privatization of most non-strategic SOEs**
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint
  - Date: 2024-05-14
  - URL: [https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-unveils-broader-plan-to-sell-most-state-owned-firms/2084587/](https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-unveils-broader-plan-to-sell-most-state-owned-firms/2084587/)
  - Claim: Sharif publicly committed to privatizing most state-owned enterprises and framed it as fiscal repair. That is concrete movement toward a long-running economic reform program.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `7B.10`

- **Aurangzeb appointment signaled technocratic staffing**
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint
  - Date: 2024-03-11
  - URL: [https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-to-choose-banker-aurangzeb-as-finance-minister-sources-say/1996592/](https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-to-choose-banker-aurangzeb-as-finance-minister-sources-say/1996592/)
  - Claim: Sharif chose a career banker rather than a party loyalist to run finance. That is strong evidence that he moved the economic portfolio toward credibility and execution capacity.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `7B.10`

- **BISP digital-wallet rollout reduced leakage and discretion**
  - Publisher: APP
  - Date: 2024-03-18
  - URL: [https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/)
  - Claim: Moving welfare payments onto digital wallets reduced leakage, delay, and discretion. This is a concrete administrative reform that makes the social-protection program more durable and less patronage-driven.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `7B.10`

- **Power-contract renegotiation improved the cost structure**
  - Publisher: Reuters via Dawn
  - Date: 2024-10-10
  - URL: [https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298](https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298)
  - Claim: The government renegotiated expensive power contracts and said it would save about Rs60 billion yearly. This is a tangible corrective action that moved policy in the direction of the stated economic program.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `7B.10`

- **Coalition bargaining kept power procedurally contestable**
  - Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint
  - Date: 2024-02-21
  - URL: [https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-largest-parties-strike-deal-on-coalition-government/1973213/](https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-largest-parties-strike-deal-on-coalition-government/1973213/)
  - Claim: After the hung election, PML-N and PPP formed a formal coalition government. This is weak but real evidence that Sharif advanced his return to office through bargaining rather than outright seizure.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`

- **Inquiry commission after judges alleged ISI intimidation**
  - Publisher: Reuters via Al Jazeera
  - Date: 2024-03-28
  - URL: [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says)
  - Claim: The government said it would form an inquiry commission after judges alleged intimidation by the ISI. This is limited, but it shows some willingness to surface a politically sensitive abuse claim instead of burying it.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`

- **Education emergency and numeric target showed a concrete social program**
  - Publisher: Radio Pakistan
  - Date: 2024-05-08
  - URL: [https://www.radio.gov.pk/08-05-2024/pm-declares-education-emergency-to-enroll-26-million-out-of-school-children](https://www.radio.gov.pk/08-05-2024/pm-declares-education-emergency-to-enroll-26-million-out-of-school-children)
  - Claim: Sharif declared an education emergency, set a numeric enrollment target, and said he would personally supervise it. That shows programmatic focus and execution intent, even if not proof of full delivery.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `7B.10`

**Counterevidence**

- **Poverty still rose even as growth recovered**
  - Publisher: World Bank
  - Date: 2024-10-10
  - URL: [https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank)
  - Claim: The macro recovery did not translate into broad household gains; poverty still increased. That limits how far one can say Sharif had advanced his program by year-end.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `7B.10`

- **IMF still said major structural problems remained**
  - Publisher: IMF
  - Date: 2024-10-10
  - URL: [https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152)
  - Claim: Pakistan still had a narrow tax base, weak governance, low investment, and insufficient health and education spending. The program was moving forward, but the end state was still far from achieved.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `7B.10`

- **Election-day shutdown undercut clean contestability**
  - Publisher: Amnesty International
  - Date: 2024-02-08
  - URL: [https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/)
  - Claim: Amnesty condemned the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation. That weakens any claim that Sharif’s rise was accompanied by a cleaner, more legitimate political order.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`

- **Protest law tightened state control over dissent**
  - Publisher: Amnesty International
  - Date: 2024-09-09
  - URL: [https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/)
  - Claim: Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded restriction powers. That is evidence of regime consolidation through coercive control, not durable institutional progress.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`

- **PTI crackdown showed coercive opposition management**
  - Publisher: Human Rights Watch
  - Date: 2024-10-09
  - URL: [https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent)
  - Claim: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and internet cuts against PTI protesters. This suggests Sharif’s government preserved itself through repression more than by broadening legitimate support.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`

- **26th Amendment weakened judicial independence**
  - Publisher: The Guardian
  - Date: 2024-10-21
  - URL: [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps)
  - Claim: Critics said the amendment weakened judicial independence and passed amid intimidation allegations. That cuts against durable institutional consolidation.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`

- **State blocked X during the election period**
  - Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com
  - Date: 2024-04-17
  - URL: [https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313)
  - Claim: The government confirmed blocking X on national-security grounds. That is information control, not a sign of a cleaner or more legitimate political trajectory.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`

- **Media pressure deepened self-censorship**
  - Publisher: Human Rights Watch
  - Date: 2024-01-11
  - URL: [https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent)
  - Claim: HRW said the government clamped down on media, opposition, and NGOs, deepening self-censorship and fear. That is negative evidence for durable institutionalization and against a broad “closer to the program” judgment outside the economic file.
  - Question IDs: `8B.10`, `8B.9`

**Search gap**
- I found strong primary-source evidence for the economic and external-policy track, and strong NGO/press evidence for domestic repression.
- I did **not** find equally strong direct evidence that Sharif had achieved durable power consolidation by end-2024; the best positives are procedural coalition formation and a few inquiries.
- I also did not find much direct evidence on long-term ideological transformation beyond the economic stabilization agenda and the stated diplomatic/nuclear restraint line.

**Best synthesis**
Sharif ended 2024 **closer to his revealed economic program** than he began, mainly through stabilization, technocratic staffing, and selected reforms. But he was **not equally closer** on the political or institutional side, where repression and judicial/media pressure remained prominent.
